hints.content: Losing mass at a rate of $10\%$ per millennium means the sample keeps $100\%-10\%=90\%$ of its mass each millennium.
So each millennium, the size is multiplied by $90\%$, which is the same as a factor of $0.9$.

If we start with the initial mass, $600$ grams, and keep multiplying by $0.9$, this function gives us the mass of the sample $t$ millennia from now:

$S(t)=600(0.9)^t$
